problem: Navigation VLAs lack large-scale, goal-dense, obstacle-aware supervision: existing robot datasets give one sparse trajectory per scene and poor coverage of close-range clutter, so policies learn goal-agnostic shortcuts and unsafe paths. Prior video-based methods (e.g., LeLaN) label trajectories with a pretrained policy whose obstacle avoidance bounds label quality.
motivation: Egocentric internet video is abundant and diverse (cluttered scenes, natural motion) but has no actions, goals, or robot-frame trajectories. Classical planners give geometric safety but need online mapping and lack semantics; VLAs give semantics but lack geometric safety. Reconstructing geometry from monocular video and using it only at training time can distill planner-level obstacle avoidance into an RGB-only VLA.
key_idea: Reconstruct local metric geometry (point map, visibility-aware ESDF) from action-free egocentric video, sample multimodal goals, generate obstacle-aware MPPI trajectories to them, and use these to train a flow-matching VLA that needs only RGB and a goal at inference.
insight: Geometry-derived supervision (ESDF-based MPPI with clearance and collision costs) gives many goal-conditioned, collision-free trajectories per frame, so the policy learns clearance without geometry at test time. Results show VEGA lowers collision rate and raises clearance versus OmniVLA, NaVILA and pi0.5 while progress stays comparable (0.31 vs 0.35). Qualitatively, baselines collapse to similar trajectories across different goals while VEGA adapts. No ablations isolate the components, so the causal claims rest on baseline comparisons.
method: Geometry recovery: MoGe-2 estimates a metric point map per frame; RANSAC ground-plane fit levels it; height-filtered points are rasterized into a BEV occupancy grid.
Visibility-aware ESDF: raytracing gives known-free/occupied/unknown space; a signed distance field is positive in free space and negative in occupied or unknown space.

Multimodal goal anchoring: Florence-2 detects objects, whose boxes are lifted through the point map to ground-plane waypoints, giving aligned text/box/waypoint goals; auxiliary waypoints are sampled from free space.

MPPI trajectory generation: 8192 rollouts x 5 iterations, unicycle dynamics, 5 s horizon, with goal, clearance (0.35 m margin, 0.5 m robot radius), collision (weight 5000), control and smoothness costs; the best collision-free or partial trajectory becomes the label.

Multimodal goal-conditioned VLA: builds on pi0.5 (SigLIP + Gemma + flow-matching action expert) to predict H x 2 local waypoint chunks; text goals go through the language model, image-region goals through frozen SigLIP, waypoint goals through a trainable MLP encoder.
Training: the VLM and vision encoders are frozen; only the waypoint encoder and waypoint action expert are trained with a flow-matching loss on MPPI targets.
Deployment: ROS 2 stack (model runner, path manager, low-level planner from CHOP) on a Ghost Robotics Vision 60 quadruped, with asynchronous inference.

setting.backbone: pi0.5 (SigLIP + Gemma backbone frozen; waypoint encoder and flow-matching action expert trained)
setting.training_data: Trajectories generated from unlabeled in-the-wild egocentric videos (walking tours, bike rides, first-person footage); VEGA-Bench dataset of about 250k scenes and 5M goal-conditioned trajectories, with a held-out test set
setting.observation: monocular RGB (current frame only, memoryless) plus goal; odometry used in deployment
setting.action_space: predicted local 2D waypoint chunks (H x 2) tracked by a low-level planner
setting.simulator: none (offline VEGA-Bench ESDF evaluation) and real world
setting.privileged: none at test time (geometry used only for training labels; VEGA-Bench evaluation uses scene ESDF)

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks are reported; results are on the paper's own VEGA-Bench and 3 real-world scenarios with 5 trials each. Table (b) values are coarse (few trials).
results: On VEGA-Bench, VEGA reaches comparable goal progress (0.31 vs OmniVLA's best 0.35) while cutting collisions to 4.52 vs 6.75 (33.0% lower) and raising clearance to 2.77 vs 2.35 (17.9% higher) over the strongest baseline, OmniVLA. In real-world trials on a quadruped, VEGA achieves success 1.0/0.6/1.0 against OmniVLA's 0.4/0.0/0.0, with fewer collisions and higher clearance. The paper claims at least 150% higher success, 66.7% fewer collisions and 60% higher clearance in real-world trials.
limitations: Policy is memoryless (current RGB and goal only), so it is brittle when goals or obstacles leave the field of view.
ESDF supervision is static and does not model dynamic obstacle motion.
Evaluation is small (5 trials per real-world scenario, 3 scenarios), with no ablations of the geometry pipeline, data scale or goal modalities.
